{{Short description|FIFA World Cup group}} {{pp-protected|small=yes}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}} {{Use American English|date=November 2025}} '''Group A''' of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] is taking place from June 11 to 24, 2026.{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}} The group consists of [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] (co-host), [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa]], [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]], and the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]]. The top two teams, and possibly the third-placed team, will advance to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]].{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 2026 Regulations |publisher=FIFA |date=May 2025 |access-date=June 7, 2025 |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623212158/https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/636f5c9c6f29771f/original/FWC2026_regulations_EN.pdf |url-status=live}} ==Teams== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- !rowspan=2| Draw position !rowspan=2| Team !rowspan=2| Pot !rowspan=2| Confederation !rowspan=2| Method of

of 32]]: * The winner of Group A will advance to play the third-placed team of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group C|Group C]], [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group E|Group E]], [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group F|Group F]], [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group H|Group H]], or [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group I|Group I]]. * The runner-up of Group A will advance to play the runner-up of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B|Group B]]. * The third-placed team of Group A might advance to play the winner of [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group E|Group E]] or [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group G|Group G]] (if one of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-placed teams|eight best third-placed teams]] from the group stage). ==Matches== All times listed are local. ===Mexico vs South Africa=== The two teams have faced each other four times, most recently in a [[2010 FIFA World Cup Group A#South Africa vs Mexico|1–1]] draw in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] [[List of FIFA World Cup opening matches|opening match]], with South Africa as the host nation.{{cite web|title=Mexico national football team: record v South Africa |url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/mexico/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/South%20Africa|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}}{{cite web|title=Mexico vs. South Africa Head-to-Head in the World Cups|url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/head_to_head/mexico_vs_south_africa.php|website=thesoccerworldcups.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}} This match coincidentally took place exactly 16 years after, being the first opening match to be a repeat of a previous opening match (although Brazil dueled Mexico in 1950, 1954 and 1962 as part of the opening match of a World Cup, the 1954 and 1962 tournaments had multiple opening matches played simultaneously). Additionally, South Africa manager [[Hugo Broos]] and Mexico’s [[Javier Aguirre]] encountered each other on the same pitch during the [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986 World Cup]] as players for [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] and Mexico, respectively. Mexico went in front in the 9th minute when [[Julián Quiñones]] scored with a low right footed finish through the legs of South African goalkeeper [[Ronwen Williams]] from just inside the penalty area after [[Sphephelo Sithole]] was caught in possession on the edge of the penalty area by [[Erik Lira]]. It was the first time a national team from CONCACAF scored the opening goal of an edition of the FIFA World Cup.{{cite web |date=2026-06-11 |title=Julian Quinones Creates History, Becomes First Player From CONCACAF Nation To Score First Goal Of A FIFA World Cup Edition |url=https://www.news18.com/amp/sports/football/julian-quinones-creates-history-becomes-first-player-from-concacaf-nation-to-score-first-goal-of-a-fifa-world-cup-edition-10144227.html |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=News18 |publisher=Network18 |language=en}} Four minutes into the second half, South Africa's Sphephelo Sithole was sent-off after fouling Mexico's [[Brian Gutiérrez]] when he was going through on goal.{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0myn4dwvzkt|title= Mexico 2 South Africa 0|date=12 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=13 June 2026}} It was 2–0 in the 67th minute when [[Raúl Jiménez]] scored his first goal at a World Cup finals, a header at the back post to the left of the net after a cross from the right by [[Roberto Alvarado]]. In the 73rd minute, South African substitute [[Themba Zwane]] was sent off for a slap in the face of Mexican forward Roberto Alvarado. In the 92nd minute there was a third [[List of FIFA World Cup red cards|red card]] in the game with Mexican captain [[César Montes]] sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity by fouling [[Khuliso Mudau]] with Mexico going on to win the game 2–0.{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/11/mexico-south-africa-world-cup-2026-group-a-match-report|title= Raúl Jiménez seals Mexico’s win against nine-man South Africa in World Cup opener|date=12 June 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=13 June 2026}}

[[Jérôme Brisard]] ([[France Football Federation|France]]) |} ===South Korea vs Czech Republic=== [[File:South Corea-Czechia2026FWC.jpg|thumb|Pre-match anthems between [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] and [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]]]] The teams had played each other three times, most recently in a 2016 friendly, a 2–1 victory for the South Koreans.{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/czech-republic/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Korea+Republic/|title=Czech Republic national football team: record v Korea Republic|website=www.11v11.com}} The Czech Republic went in front in the 59th minute with a header from captain [[Ladislav Krejčí (footballer, born 1999)|Ladislav Krejčí]] to the right of the net from six yards out after a long throw-in from [[Vladimír Coufal]] from the right. It was 1–1 in the 67th minute when [[Hwang In-beom]] received the ball from [[Lee Kang-in]] before turning back onto his right foot before scooping the ball over the advancing Czech goalkeeper [[Matěj Kovář]] and into the right of the net.{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/12/south-korea-czechia-world-cup-2026-group-a-match-report|title= South Korea get off to winning start after rallying from goal down to beat Czechia|date=12 June 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=13 June 2026}} In the 78th minute [[Tomáš Souček]] headed into the net for the Czech Republic after a free-kick from the left, but the goal was ruled out for offside. In the 80th minute, Hwang In-beom crossed low from the right and [[Oh Hyeon-gyu]] finished from six yards out to the left of the net to put South Korea 2–1 in front. In the 82nd minute, South Korean goalkeeper [[Kim Seung-gyu]] saved down low to his right to stop [[Adam Hložek]]'s close-range effort with South Korea going on to win 2–1.{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg0vvrg70vt|title= South Korea 2 Czech Republic 1|date=12 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=13 June 2026}}
